section_1.title: Visualizing Linear Systems (1 min)
section_1.content: Introduce linear systems as transformations. A system Ax = b represents the search for an input vector 'x' that maps to a target vector 'b'. Visualize columns of 'A' as basis vectors that define the destination grid.
section_1.example: Imagine a robot arm (the matrix A) moving in 2D space. The system solves where to set the joint angles (x) to place the gripper at a target coordinate (b).

section_2.title: Column Space: The Reachable World (1 min)
section_2.content: Define Column Space as the span of the matrix columns—the set of all possible outcomes. If the columns are linearly independent, they span the full space. If they are dependent, the reach 'collapses' into a line or a point.
section_2.example: A 2D drone can fly anywhere (full column space). If its motors are locked on a specific axis, it can only move along a line (a lower-dimensional column space).

section_3.title: Null Space: The 'Ghost' Inputs (1 min)
section_3.content: Define Null Space as the set of non-zero inputs 'x' that map to the origin. These represent ambiguity or loss of information during the transformation.
section_3.example: A 3D scanner (Matrix A) takes a 3D object and projects it into a 2D image. The 'Null Space' is the line of sight along which depth is lost; any object placed on that line results in the same 2D shadow.

section_4.title: Inverse Matrices: The Rewind Button (1 min)
section_4.content: Explain the inverse matrix A⁻¹ as a 'reversal' operation. This only exists if the mapping is bijective (non-zero determinant). Geometrically, this means we can uniquely 'undo' the transformation to return to the original input.
section_4.example: A video compressor (A) makes a file smaller (mapping to a smaller space). The inverse (A⁻¹) is the decompressor that reconstructs the original video from the compressed data.

section_5.title: Synthesis & Summary (1 min)
section_5.content: Connect the dots: If the Null Space contains only zero, the system is invertible. If the Column Space doesn't cover the whole target space, the system may have no solution (b is unreachable) or infinitely many (if b is in the column space).
section_5.example: A summary animation showing a transformation (A) followed by its inverse (A⁻¹) returning to the start, highlighting that if there is a 'Null Space', the inverse path cannot be uniquely traced back.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text("- " + line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                # Shift right side area
                x = 3.5 + j * 0.8
                y = 2.2 - i * 0.8
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
